question.problem: Let $F(x,y,z)=yz\,i+xz\,j+xy\,k$ and let $C$ be a path in ${R}^{3}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$

current_example.problem: Let $\mathbf{F}(x,y) = (3x+2) \: \mathbf{i} - y^3 \: \mathbf{j}$ and let $C$ be a path in $\mathbb R^2.$ Write $\displaystyle \int\limits_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \text{d}\mathbf{r}$ in the form $\displaystyle\int_C P(x,y)\,\textrm d x +  Q(x,y)\,\textrm d y.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y) = P(x,y) \: \mathbf{i} + Q(x,y) \: \mathbf{j}
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
\int\limits_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \text{d}\mathbf{r} = \int\limits_C P(x,y) \: \text{d}x + Q(x,y) \: \text{d}y.
$$

In our case, $P = 3x+2$ and $Q = -y^3.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}(3x+2)\,\text{d}x-{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
